title.narrative: Output 8.1. Increased capacity of member States to develop new or reformed sustainable national social protection strategies, policies or legal frameworks to extend coverage and enhance benefit adequacy

description.narrative:
(1) The National Social Protection Strategy (NSPS), adopted by the Prime Minister's Decree No.224 on 1 April 2020, was officially launched and disseminated to ministries at the national and provincial levels. NSPS drafting committee held consultations with government actors, workers' organizations, employers' organizations. A roadmap (action plan) and monitoring framework for the Strategy was submitted for further discussion within the National Social Protection Commission. (2)The Mother and Early Childhood Grant (MECG) programme, was launched in June 2021, by the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare in Attapeu province. It is being piloted under the UN Joint Programme. It has enrolled 982 pregnant women and infants in the programme and provided a monthly cash benefit of Lao Kip 150,000 (US$16) to 192 beneficiaries in Sanamxay district so far. The program aims to reach at least 2000 beneficiaries in 3 districts. (3)As part of the COVID response to protect workers affected by factory closures/work stoppages, the Lao Social Security Organization (LSSO) provided, between June and August 2021, a one-time partial unemployment cash benefit (wage subsidy) to all garment sector workers amounting to US$90 per person. It was originally planned for 17,289 workers but LSSO data recorded a total number of 24,280 eligible workers. (1) Through the projects financed by the Government of Luxembourg, the ILO technically supported the development of the NSPS and the organization of national consultations, including dialogue with the social partners and UN agencies. These included (i) Capacity Building and UNJP Roadmap Discussion Workshop in Thalat from 25-27 August 2020 (approx. 30 participants); (ii) the official launch of the NSPS and UNJP in Vientiane, on 30 September 2020 (approx. 40 participants); and (iii) a Training programme on social protection policy design and implementation in Vientiane, 24-26 Nov 2020 (approx. 40 participants)
(2) The MECG program was introduced as part of the approval of the NSPS. ILO contributed to the design in partnership with UNICEF (UN Joint Programme). Additionally, the ILO provided financial and technical support for the purchase of IT equipment for the Ministry of Health and MOLSW.
With the Resident Coordinator's office, the ILO led the preparation of the UN Country team note "Developing a shock-responsive national social protection system to respond to the COVID-19 crisis in Lao PDR" presented to government.
(3) The ILO/BMZ project provided financial and technical support for the one-time partial unemployment cash benefit (wage subsidy) to all garment sector workers.

Output 8.2. Increased capacity of member States to improve governance and sustainability of social protection systems

description.narrative: The National Health Insurance Verification Guideline was developed, and it was endorsed by the Minister of Health in September 2020. The guideline will contribute to transparency in the financial management of the national health insurance and health care facilities by collecting and analyzing the data to support the calculation of health care service costs in an accurate and timely manner and ensure the quality of both fund management and hospital services as well as the satisfaction of the insured members. The ILO provided technical and financial support to the development of verification guideline. The technical support included inputs to the design of the guideline and financial support to organize two meetings with central and provincial stakeholders to discuss and finalize the guideline, and the training on the use of guideline for two southern provinces.
